question: What current-name candidates do authoritative fish catalogs support for the 13 fish labels in the Govantes River article body, without treating the names as verified sampled organisms?

method.summary: Compared only the 13 fish-name strings recorded from the article body in the companion source review with Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes indexed current-status excerpts and WoRMS accepted-name records. The Catalog's current status and historical valid-as treatments are retained where they differ. Direct Catalog page retrieval was unavailable in the web reader; the indexed excerpts were used. No publisher PDF, table image, figure, fish photograph, or data file was downloaded or retained in this crosscheck.
method.nameUseBoundary: A current-name match is nomenclatural context only. It does not identify any Govantes specimen, verify the article's station distribution, or resolve whether the body-only Lycothrissa label belongs in the missing twentieth taxon.
method.sourceScope: The crosscheck does not transcribe or reconcile the inaccessible image-only fish tables. It uses the 13 body labels already preserved in the source review and leaves the Figure 1 count conflict open.
method.reuseBoundary: The article's clear derivative-data reuse terms remain unresolved in the companion source review. This crosscheck grants no permission to reuse article tables, images, or derived rows.

sources.role: The source review's 13 body-listed fish labels; not an image-verified table transcription or specimen determination.

sources.authority: Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes, California Academy of Sciences
sources.role: Current-status and spelling candidates for 12 of the 13 body-listed fish labels. The Catalog also preserves competing valid-as treatments for Leiognathus equulus and notes possible placement of Lycothrissa crocodilus in Setipinna; neither note identifies the study fish.
sources.reviewedSections: Indexed current-status or valid-as name treatments only. No distribution, habitat, conservation, image, specimen, or occurrence evidence was imported.

sources.authority: World Register of Marine Species (WoRMS); Flanders Marine Institute
sources.role: Accepted-name crosscheck for the two ponyfish labels: Leiognathus equulus is accepted as Leiognathus equula, and Leiognathus daura is accepted as Karalla daura. These are name mappings only, not study-specimen determinations.

sourceLabelGroups.label: Leiognathus equulus
sourceLabelGroups.authorityFinding: The Catalog's current-status field gives Leiognathus equula, while its record also lists historical valid-as treatments for Leiognathus equulus. WoRMS maps Leiognathus equulus to Leiognathus equula.
sourceLabelGroups.interpretation: Record the Catalog/WoRMS name treatment as a candidate only; retain the article's exact spelling and do not resolve the specimen from nomenclature.

interpretation.sourceStringsPolicy: Keep the article's exact body strings unchanged. Store authority name mappings only in this separately attributed crosswalk; do not turn them into accepted species assertions or occurrences.
limits: The article reports 20 macrofauna taxa, including 13 fish, while the Figure 1 caption contains 19 labels; the body-only Lycothrissa crocodillus mention does not resolve the missing label or total.
The publisher table cells were not image-verified in the companion source review; this review does not infer counts or station assignments.
Exact collection dates, season, fish effort, voucher/accession identifiers, and a reproducible fish capture protocol remain unavailable in the reviewed materials.
Catalog name status does not validate any Govantes organism, historical occurrence, current presence, habitat, catchability, diet, bait suitability, safety, or fishing legality.
The article's derivative-data reuse terms remain unclear; no tables, figures, photos, or raw values were reproduced or approved.

nextAction: Keep the name crosswalk research-only. Resolve the source count/table mismatch, obtain exact sampling dates and voucher or author-linked determinations, and clarify derivative-data reuse terms before considering any app projection; continue independent Region I freshwater, brackish, and marine source discovery.
